prompt.context: Our client is a major diversified financial services firm. They have 4 lines of business: Checking Accounts, Savings Accounts, Loans, and Mortgages. The bank is profitable, but the CEO is on a mission to increase overall market share while still maintaining profitability. He is considering increasing his sales force to accomplish this. There are 3 different categories of sales force he can choose to change: Branch Managers, Telemarketers, and Mortgage Agents.
prompt.question: The CEO has come to us for advice on whether or not he should increase his sales staff, and if so, where he should be adding heads. How would you go about addressing this question?

clarifying_info.q: What does a mortgage agent actually do?
clarifying_info.a: Mortgage agents work by having relationships with real estate brokers. When a broker makes a sale, he refers the buyer of the home to a mortgage agent. That agent works with the home buyer to close the transaction and sell the mortgage.

clarifying_info.q: How many players are in the market and what is the market share breakdown? Is everyone profitable? Are there any new entrants or trends like internet banking?
clarifying_info.a: The market is made up of 5 major players. They are all very similar, offering diversified services and playing in all 4 segments. The #1 player has 20% market share. We are the #2 player with 18% market share. The rest of the industry is somewhere between 15%-18%. Everyone is profitable and established and no one is pricing their products irrationally. Some new trends like internet banking are emerging but are not a factor at this point and the CEO is not worried about that.

clarifying_info.q: How does our market share break down in each of the different segments?
clarifying_info.a: Checking Accounts: 21%, Business Accounts: 20%, Loans: 23%, Mortgages: 10%.

clarifying_info.q: Is there a different profitability level for each of the different segments?
clarifying_info.a: Profit per transaction: Checking Accounts $5, Business Accounts $20, Loans $100, Mortgages $1,000.

clarifying_info.q: How are telemarketers generating their profits?
clarifying_info.a: They call up existing customers to get them to renew their old services.

clarifying_info.q: How many customers come through each branch and what is the breakdown of new vs. existing?
clarifying_info.a: Each store has 4 branch managers and they on average service 40 potential new customers that come through the door every day (10 per manager).

exhibits.title: Sales Force Profitability
exhibits.shows: A bar chart comparing the profitability (in $K of incremental profit margin) of three sales categories — Branch Managers, Mortgage Agents, and Telemarketers — broken down by Existing Customers and New Business.
exhibits.data: Y-axis: Profitability ($K), range 0-250. Three grouped bars: Branch Managers (Existing Customers and New Business, both relatively low), Mortgage Agents (New Business bar is notably high, Existing Customers low), Telemarketers (Existing Customers bar is the largest of all, New Business very small). Telemarketers have the highest total profitability overall.

framework: 1. Determine the competitive position of the company: overall market structure, number of players, market share breakdown, pricing behavior.
2. Assess the importance of each line of business: market share by segment, profitability per transaction by segment, strategic fit and growth potential in each segment.

3. Understand the impact of each sales force category: which lines of business each category affects, ROI and incremental profit per additional hire in each category, whether gains come from new customers or existing customers.
4. Formulate an investment strategy: recommend where to add sales heads based on market share gap, per-transaction profitability, and the CEO's explicit goal of growing market share.

questions.prompt: What is the competitive landscape and what does our current market position tell us?
questions.guidance: 5 major players, all diversified and present in all 4 segments. We are #2 overall with 18% share (vs. #1 at 20%). The market is stable — no irrational pricing. Segment-level share differs from overall share. The key insight is that the overall market is fairly tight (15-20% range), suggesting limited room to grab share in mature segments but possibly more room in mortgage where our share (10%) is well below our overall position.

questions.prompt: Which line of business offers the most attractive opportunity for market share growth?
questions.guidance: Compare segment share to overall share: Checking 21%, Business Accounts 20%, Loans 23% — all near or above our 18% overall share. Mortgages at 10% are well below our overall share, indicating significant underperformance. Profit per transaction is highest for Mortgages ($1,000 vs. $100 for Loans, $20 for Business Accounts, $5 for Checking). Candidate should conclude mortgages represent the biggest gap and highest reward per transaction.

math.setup: Compare profit per transaction across segments: Mortgages $1,000 vs. Loans $100 vs. Business Accounts $20 vs. Checking Accounts $5. Mortgages are 10x more profitable per transaction than Loans and 200x more than Checking.
math.answer: Mortgages are by far the highest-value segment per transaction, and our 10% share leaves the most room to grow relative to the 20-23% share held in other segments.

questions.prompt: Given the exhibit on Sales Force Profitability, which sales channel should the CEO invest in to increase market share?
questions.guidance: The chart shows Telemarketers have the highest total profitability, but almost entirely from Existing Customers (renewals). Mortgage Agents generate the highest New Business profitability. Branch Managers contribute modestly in both categories. Since the CEO's goal is to increase market share (i.e., win new customers), Mortgage Agents are the right investment — they drive new business in the highest-value segment. Telemarketers are better for profitability from existing customers but do not grow market share.

questions.prompt: Under what circumstances would adding more Branch Managers make sense?
questions.guidance: Study each branch to measure: (1) volume of potential new customers coming through the door each day, and (2) whether existing managers are at capacity. With 4 managers and 40 new walk-in customers per day, each manager handles 10 customers. If managers are not at capacity (no long wait times, no customers leaving), adding a 5th manager reduces load to 8 per manager but creates idle time without generating new customers. Adding managers makes sense if: wait times are long and potential customers are leaving, or if new initiatives (new product launch, advertising campaign) drive more foot traffic that exceeds current manager capacity.

math.setup: 4 branch managers, 40 potential new customers per day.
steps: Adding a 5th manager: 40 / 5 = 8 customers per manager per day — creates slack if current managers can already handle 10
math.answer: Unless current managers are overloaded or foot traffic grows, adding a 5th branch manager creates idle capacity and does not increase new customer acquisition.

brainstorming.prompt: What scenarios or changes in the business environment could justify adding more branch managers in the future?

categories.name: Demand-side drivers
ideas: A new advertising campaign that drives significantly more foot traffic into branches
Launch of a new product that attracts non-customers to visit branches
A market trend that shifts customer preference back toward in-person banking

categories.name: Capacity constraints
ideas: Evidence of long wait times causing potential customers to leave without being served
Customer satisfaction data showing poor in-branch experience due to understaffing
Data showing a high drop-off rate of walk-in prospects before being served

categories.name: Competitive dynamics
ideas: A competitor closing branches in a geography, redirecting their customers to our branches
A new segment of customers (e.g., small business owners) that prefers branch interaction

recommendation: The CEO should increase his sales force, and should focus the investment on Mortgage Agents.

Mortgages represent our weakest segment (10% share vs. 18-23% in all other segments) and the highest profit per transaction ($1,000). Mortgage agents are the only sales channel that generates meaningful new customer acquisition in this segment, making them the right lever to grow market share while maintaining profitability.
risks: Adding mortgage agents increases cost; if real estate referral pipelines are insufficient, agents may be underutilized.
Mortgage market share gains may take time to materialize as broker relationships need to be built.
Over-investment in one segment could leave other lines of business under-resourced.
next_steps: Quantify the number of real estate broker relationships available in each target market to estimate the capacity for new mortgage agent hires.
Model the payback period for each new mortgage agent hire given the $1,000 per transaction profit.
Monitor Telemarketer ROI on existing customers separately as a profitability lever distinct from the market share growth initiative.
